The Global Fund case study says HealthTech Hub Africa, a pan-African health tech accelerator co-funded by the Global Fund and others, is based in Kigali at Norrsken House, with no startup cohort or programme described.
RISA's Hanga Hubs page says the project established incubation hubs and runs a nine-month cohort programme (ideation, pre-incubation, incubation) for young entrepreneurs, listed as ongoing.
RISA says Hanga Hubs were set up in seven districts: Musanze, Rwamagana, Huye, Muhanga, Nyagatare, Rubavu and Rusizi.

MINICT's page says Kigali Innovation City, a USD 2 billion project in Kigali's Special Economic Zone, is set to host universities, technology companies and startups on 70 hectares, with Africa50 committing USD 400 million.

The ministry's ICT Hub Strategy 2019-2024 assigns an ICT Incubation responsibility to offer incubation facilities to start-ups, including office space and basic technology infrastructure, and lists a priority-2 project for 2022-2024 to build expertise in ICT business incubation.

The ministry's ICT Sector Strategic Plan 2018-2024 says Kigali Innovation City, a space for incubation centres, companies and innovation centres, is currently underway, and plans a business incubation centre and an innovation fund.

The ministry's ICT Sector Strategic Plan 2018-2024 says the ICT Chamber established kLab in 2011 as an innovation centre that connects, nurtures and introduces potential entrepreneurs to ICT opportunities, and a FabLab maker space in 2016; no programme or cohort is stated.

The Smart City Rwanda Masterplan, developed in 2017, says plans are underway to establish the Kigali Innovation City, an innovation park on the outskirts of Kigali linked to academia, government and industry.

The Smart Rwanda 2020 Master Plan lists an ICT Innovation Center project of USD 5.6 million with a 24-month duration led by RDB, a Kigali Innovation City, an ICT innovation fund for 100 start-ups and a women and girls in ICT incubation programme.
